title: Keep /cv and /en/cv at zero client JavaScript: production PDFs are printed from the PUBLISHED pages
body: functions/cv.pdf.ts and functions/en/cv.pdf.ts call functions/_handler.ts, which asks Cloudflare Browser Rendering to print the live /cv or /en/cv and waits for network idle (`LOAD_WAIT` in scripts/pdf-options.ts: networkidle0 on Browser Rendering, networkidle on Playwright). Any script on those pages — a component with a <script>, an island, analytics added to src/layouts/Base.astro, a ClientRouter — changes the downloaded PDF silently in production, not just your local build. Only the two landings (index.html, en/index.html) may ship JS; the allowlist is `PAGES_WITH_JS` in scripts/pages-with-js.ts, and adding a page there is an explicit decision that must show up in a diff, never a fix for a failing `pnpm run test:js`. Put landing-only scripts in src/pages/index.astro / src/pages/en/index.astro, never in Base.astro or src/components/cv/** (shared with the CV pages).
not_derivable: The link between 'a script in Base.astro' and 'a different PDF in production' spans the layout, the Pages Function and the print options; nothing in Base.astro or the CV components warns about it.

evidence.summary: Header: source page must stay at zero JS in either locale; a script now breaks the PDF in production.
PAGES_WITH_JS = index.html, en/index.html; shared by no-client-js and bundle-budget checks.
LOAD_WAIT: networkidle0 vs networkidle, shared by local render and the Function.
